page: Microsoft Azure E48ps_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on an ARM64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, delivering a memory density of 8.0 GB per core. It contains no dedicated GPU accelerators and features zero local storage, requiring remote storage volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems and disk IO.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio targets workloads requiring extensive RAM allocations alongside parallel computing capacity. While modern x86 extended instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AMX, and specific x86 cryptography extensions are not present due to the ARM architecture, the dedicated vCPU allocation ensures predictable processing throughput without noisy-neighbor contention.

From an efficiency perspective, ARM-based cloud instances often provide favorable operating efficiency and resource density compared to traditional x86 alternatives. A notable architectural tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral NVMe disks and bundled public IPv4 networking, necessitating external storage configurations and network mapping. The server is well suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications compiled for the ARM64 platform.
